donationText:
365 days a year, PAWS responds to calls involving abused, neglected, injured, and abandoned animals. From emergency rescues and medical treatment to shelter care, rehabilitation, and finding loving homes, every life saved is possible because of compassionate supporters.

Many rescued animals require extensive veterinary treatment and prolonged shelter care. Your contribution helps meet medical expenses, maintain our rescue centre, and continue lifesaving care.

stories.title: Vaccination and Awareness Programmes to Celebrate World Rabies Day
stories.body:
Observed on **28th September, World Rabies Day** reminds us that rabies is a lethal but preventable disease. India remains one of the countries most affected by rabies, making vaccination and awareness essential. To mark the occasion, **PAWS, in collaboration with Mission Rabies, conducted a two-day mega Anti-Rabies Vaccination drive on 27th and 28th September in Badlapur, vaccinating a total of 360 community animals.**

Alongside the vaccination drive, PAWS and Mission Rabies conducted awareness programmes at **South Indian Education Center, Badlapur, and Adarsh College, Badlapur.** Students were sensitised about rabies, the dos and don'ts when interacting with community animals, and how to respond safely when encountering an aggressive dog. Together, these initiatives reinforced the message that **rabies can be prevented through vaccination, awareness, and responsible action.**

stories.title: Equipping Animal Caregivers with the Skills to Save Lives
stories.body:
On **12th September 2026, PAWS organised a First Aid Training Session** to mark World First Aid Day. Senior veterinarian **Dr. Dilip Choudhary** guided participants on basic first aid, essential dos and don'ts, and emergency care for animals in distress. The session was followed by guidance from **Dr. Nilesh Bhanage** on addressing society-level concerns, dealing with human-animal conflict, and becoming a responsible caregiver for community animals.

The session brought together **30 animal lovers and volunteers**, who received **first-aid kits and certificates** upon completion. The training helped participants understand how timely and appropriate first aid can make a crucial difference when an animal is injured or in distress.

stories.title: Wildlife Rescue of the Month
stories.subtitle: A Second Chance for an Injured Green Vine Snake
stories.body:
In September, **PAWS rescued a total of 36 wild animals, including 16 birds, 18 snakes, and 2 other reptiles.** The rescues included species such as House Crow, Rock Pigeon, Night Heron, Red-whiskered Bulbul, White-breasted Waterhen, Spectacled Cobra, Common Wolf Snake, Checkered Keelback, Buff-striped Keelback, Rat Snake, Green Vine Snake, Indian Softshell Turtle, and Monitor Lizard.

Among these, the rescue of a **three-foot-long Green Vine Snake from Dombivli West** stood out. Reported as injured, the snake was found with a severe wound to its head, appearing to have been attacked by another animal. PAWS volunteer **Rishikesh Surse** immediately rescued the snake and took it to the **Kalyan Forest Department for treatment and further rehabilitation.**

Snakes and birds are often frightened of humans and generally try to escape when encountered. If you come across an injured or distressed wild animal, **do not panic, harm, or attempt to kill it.** Instead, contact the nearest wildlife rescue organisation or government helpline for assistance. A calm and responsible response can help protect both the animal and people around it.

stories.title: Community Animal Rescue Story of the Month
stories.subtitle: A Second Chance for an Old Dog
stories.body:
In September, **PAWS rescued a total of 46 community animals - 44 dogs and 2 cats.** Among these rescues was an old black female dog who had a **massive tumour on her belly** that had grown to an alarming size. Due to her age and temperament, performing the required surgery posed additional challenges, but the tumour was growing rapidly and needed immediate attention. PAWS stepped in, rescued her, and arranged for the tumour to be surgically removed.

Following the surgery, the dog received extended post-operative care until her wound and sutures had completely healed. She was then **safely released back to her original area.** If you come across a sick or injured community animal in your locality, please do not ignore it. These animals often depend on timely intervention for their survival. Contact your nearest animal welfare organisation and help ensure that they receive the care they need.

stories.title: Empowering Students to Care for Animals
stories.body:
During September 2026, **PAWS conducted five awareness programmes across Mumbai, reaching a total of 261 students.** The sessions covered rabies awareness, animal welfare, and the importance of student-led animal welfare initiatives, encouraging young people to take meaningful action for animals in their schools and colleges.

PAWS believes that empowering students with knowledge can help create a more compassionate and responsible generation. **If your school or college in Mumbai would like to conduct an animal welfare awareness programme, reach out to PAWS** - we would be happy to help empower students to make a difference for animals.

stories.title: 540+ Community Animals Protected Against Rabies
stories.body:
During September 2026, **PAWS organised three anti-rabies vaccination drives across the KDMC, Ambernath, and Badlapur municipal council areas, vaccinating more than 540 community animals.** These drives form an important part of PAWS' ongoing efforts to protect community animals and strengthen rabies prevention at the grassroots level.

Rabies is a lethal but preventable disease, and vaccination remains one of the most effective tools in preventing its spread. Alongside awareness and education, PAWS continues to actively vaccinate community animals across the region, working towards the larger goal of a **rabies-free India where both animals and communities can live safer lives.**

stories.title: Feeding Community Animals, Continuing Raju's Legacy
stories.body:
In September 2026, **PAWS distributed a total of 150 kg of dog food** to feeders and animal caretakers across **Badlapur**, helping provide meals to approximately **750 community animals.**

This feeding initiative continues in loving memory of **Raju**, an indie dog who grew to become a beloved companion, protector, and familiar face in his community. Cared for by countless compassionate people throughout his life, Raju's legacy continues to inspire kindness and care towards community animals.

Every meal shared is a tribute to Raju and a reminder that compassion can live on through the lives we continue to care for.
